lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Capitol Hill, 2031. The public gallery is full. The floor is not: forty members out of six hundred, most of them reading something else. On the order paper is a private member's bill at its third reading.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: The Enabling Bill. Eleven pages. Nobody outside this building has heard of it and nobody inside it has read past the long title.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: What it does is create a legal category. Perpetual administrative counterparty. A thing that can be a party to a contract with no end date attached to it.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: That means nothing to me, and I can tell from your face that it should.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: It means a thing can be owned forever. Not for ninety-nine years, not for the life of a person, not until somebody dies or a company folds. Forever, by whoever is holding the paper.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Every question I have been chasing for three centuries hangs off this room, this afternoon, and it will be over in about eleven minutes.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Eleven pages, third reading, Thursday afternoon, on the nod. That is not carelessness, that is the method. I have watched it done nine times and I have never once been able to prove it was done on purpose.
